solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Idea not supposed to impress supervisors, alluded to previously

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so one set of letters is pushed inside the other
supposed in the sense of imagined or made up, so the letters of these two words are reinvented in a new order

parts.note: foremen supervise workers on a site or shop floor

explanation.surface: A notion that was never meant to sway the bosses, already hinted at earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supposed' makes ATIONED from IDEA NOT, and 'to impress' sets FOREMEN within it, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something already referred to earlier in a text has been mentioned before.

clue.text: Evergreen nation welcoming male officer on ship

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen conifer

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A country of pine forests takes in a man who serves as a ship's officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The deck officer next in rank below the captain on a merchant vessel.

clue.text: River, perfect river

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
to hone is to sharpen or perfect a skill

explanation.surface: Praise of a flawless waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a major French river flowing from the Alps to the Mediterranean via Lyon.

clue.text: Massive outlet feeding biodome, gas to release

indicators.note: the run of letters is fed into the words that follow, sitting within them across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A huge retail chain is supplying a biodome, which needs gas let out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a shop, and a massive one is a very large store selling many lines.

clue.text: Straight over brow of hill, Welsh town

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a straight drink is neat, without mixer

indicators.note: the brow is the top of the hill, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Straight over the crest of a hill lies a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a town in South Wales near Swansea, in the Vale of the same name.

clue.text: Behind upstanding king and queen, pair listening?

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
a rani is a Hindu queen or a rajah's wife
ears come in a pair and do the listening

explanation.surface: A royal couple stand while a pair eavesdrop from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' makes INARR; a rani is an Indian queen, not the usual R or ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a payer who is behind with what is owed has fallen late on payments.

clue.text: Circular loop, end of rope just round the corner pulled up

indicators.note: pulled up in a down entry means the letters are read upward
the end of the word rope is its final letter

parts.note: something just round the corner is coming soon

explanation.surface: A circle of rope whose end is about to be hauled tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a running loop in a rope that tightens when pulled, as on a hangman's rope or lasso.

clue.text: One putting things on sideboard

definitions.meaning: someone who puts clothes on another, as in a theatre wardrobe
a kitchen cabinet with shelves for plates above drawers

explanation.surface: Someone setting objects on a piece of dining furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who clothes an actor, and a kitchen cupboard with open shelving.

clue.text: One found in bed perhaps, flies originally down

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word flies

parts.note: to lower something is to bring it down

explanation.surface: Something in a bed where insects first came down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not one for sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: blooms are grown in garden beds, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Slowly travel east of Clare, avoiding the outskirts

indicators.note: in an across entry east is to the right, so this piece follows
skipping the outer letters of the name leaves its middle

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Take your time driving through Clare without the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare is an Irish county as well as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction: an Italian tempo marking meaning broad and slow.

clue.text: Dip a tea plant, mile off, into liquid glue

indicators.note: into tells us the pieces go inside the mixed letters
a liquid state suggests flowing and reforming, so the letters are mixed
off means the following word is removed

parts.note: camomile is a plant brewed as a herbal tea
the word mile is taken out as written

explanation.surface: Plunge a herb into runny adhesive, a mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' turns GLUE into GU..LE; 'off' leaves CAMO from CAMOMILE, so A + CAMO goes 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Mexican avocado sauce served as a dip with tortilla chips.

clue.text: Bit of a nag dies slowly

definitions.meaning: the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades, nag being an old horse
shrivels and fades away, like a plant

explanation.surface: An old horse that is gradually fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the high point of a horse's back, and a verb for drying up and wasting.

clue.text: Couple run around naked at first, on ship

indicators.note: on means placed next to the following piece
around means the first piece goes about the next

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of naked

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Two people streak about nude aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to yoke or hitch together, as horses to a cart.

clue.text: Animal found in the water butt

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family
the stub end of a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A creature living in the rainwater barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water butt' is a rain barrel, but 'butt' stands alone as the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a silvery river fish, and slang for a smoked joint's end.

clue.text: Dim recollection in desire for something else

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: a hunger is a craving or desire

indicators.note: read as re-collection, the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A faint memory of craving for something different.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: 'something else' means something remarkable, a real cracker.

clue.text: Splash of red, almost a work of art

indicators.note: splashing scatters the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A dab of red paint nearly makes a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by a leading European artist from before about 1800, or the artist.

clue.text: It is hidden under plate — bloody shame

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits below the others

parts.note: a disc is a flat plate
red is the colour of blood

explanation.surface: Something is concealed beneath a dish, a dreadful disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dishonour or loss of reputation.

clue.text: Soften mood finally during rite seen as grotesque

indicators.note: during puts that letter inside the other piece
grotesque means misshapen, so these letters are distorted
finally picks the last letter of mood

explanation.surface: A bizarre ritual eventually changes the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as grotesque' turns RITE SEEN into TENERISE, with D set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make meat less tough by beating or marinating.

clue.text: So deep in sleep in centre of bed without short trousers?

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so one piece pockets another

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, as is a dram

indicators.note: takes the middle letter of bed

parts.note: less means lacking or without

explanation.surface: Sleeping soundly in bed, with no shorts on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb, to pocket: DRAM takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep untroubled by any visions is the deepest kind of rest.

clue.text: Noble knight mostly on the game

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits on top of the next
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to dub is to knight with a tap of the sword
chess is the game in which a knight is a piece

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady plays a game with nearly a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman of high rank, the wife of a duke.

clue.text: Setter is back in hole

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the sun is something that sets

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler is back in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, but is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: a cavity in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Model, one rarely missed?

definitions.meaning: someone who poses for an artist or photographer
an easy catch or chance in sport

explanation.surface: A model whose absence is seldom noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an artist's poser, and an easy opportunity in ball games.

clue.text: Apple, little one underwater?

explanation.surface: An apple fallen into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an elongated cooking apple, and a young cod.

clue.text: Sink blocked at the bottom, rubbish coming up

indicators.note: the bottom of the word blocked is its final letter
coming up in a down entry means read upward

parts.note: poor and rubbish both mean of low quality

explanation.surface: A blocked sink with waste rising up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like a basin; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sag or slump downward.

clue.text: Criticise access

definitions.meaning: to nag or carp at someone

explanation.surface: Finding fault with the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the phrasal verb: to find fault with, and to reach.

clue.text: Regard muscle during period of relaxation

indicators.note: during puts it inside the other piece

parts.note: a rest is a period of relaxation
a pec is a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Consider working a muscle during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: esteem or high opinion.

clue.text: Little bird seemingly quite upset, attacking bunting initially

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A small bird appears rattled as it goes for a bunting.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunting is a small finch-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a young pigeon not yet fledged.

clue.text: Happy about nothing, no good going further

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: elated means very happy
O is the zero digit, nothing

explanation.surface: Pleased about having nothing, and no good at advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stretched out or extended farther.

clue.text: Link every second part in turn, and tie in knots

indicators.note: takes the second and fourth letters of turn
knotted letters are twisted, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Join every other part in turn and tie the knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to join or connect things together.

clue.text: In a storm at sea, plebs screening rank drama

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or around, so it goes inside
a storm tosses the letters about

parts.note: to rank is to rate

explanation.surface: Common folk on a ship in rough weather, a dramatic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A 1954 play by Terence Rattigan set in a seaside hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Rattigan's two-part play set in a Bournemouth hotel dining room.
